blocks.text: The five d orbitals are dxy, dxz, dyz, dx2-y2 and dz2. They have a characteristic cloverleaf shape, generally like four lobes or two dumbbells in a plane. In an isolated atom all five have the same energy: they are degenerate. Their shapes and directions decide the bonding, colour and magnetic properties of transition metals.

blocks.title: Degenerate and non-degenerate orbitals
blocks.text: Degenerate orbitals have the same energy. When ligands approach a metal ion to form a complex, their electric field splits the five d orbitals into two sets of different energy (non-degenerate). The energy gap between the sets is written delta E.
In an octahedral complex (six ligands), such as [Ti(H2O)6]3+, the d orbitals split into three lower-energy orbitals (dxy, dxz, dyz) and two higher-energy orbitals (dx2-y2, dz2).

blocks.alt: Energy diagram with an upward Energy axis. Degenerate Orbitals: five equal boxes dxy, dyz, dzx, dx2-y2, dz2 with one electron. Ligands interaction: the five boxes raised. They then split: dx2-y2 and dz2 above, dxy, dyz and dzx below holding the electron, separated by Delta E. Light is absorbed and, after Excitation, the electron is in the upper set.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.4: Splitting of d orbitals in octahedral fields (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.4).

blocks.text: In a tetrahedral complex (four ligands), such as [CuCl4]2-, the splitting is inverted: three higher-energy orbitals (dxy, dxz, dyz) and two lower-energy orbitals (dx2-y2, dz2). The splitting is smaller than in octahedral complexes.

blocks.alt: Energy diagram for nine d electrons. Degenerate orbitals: five equal boxes, four with paired electrons and one with a single electron. Ligands interaction: the boxes raised. Split: dxy, dyz, dzx above (paired, paired, single) and dx2-y2, dz2 below (both paired), separated by Delta E. Light is absorbed and, after Excitation, the upper set is full and the lower set has one single electron.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.5: Splitting of d orbitals in tetrahedral fields (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.5).
